name: Planning Poker
highLevelGoals: The Moderator aims to efficiently create, manage, and guide estimation sessions to help the team collectively set sprint goals.
The Moderator seeks to add, edit, delete, and re-estimate items for estimation with ease, adapting to evolving team understanding.
The Moderator desires functionalities to quickly accept estimates, import stories, browse previous games, and export game transcripts for record-keeping and analysis.
The Moderator expects to securely create, log in, modify, and delete their account details, including password recovery options.
The Moderator aims to configure game settings such as estimation scales and the number of estimators to best suit their team's preferences and size.
The Estimator aims to join games, view items for estimation, and submit their estimates effectively.
The Estimator seeks to see all items to be estimated, view who has given estimates, and understand the current state of the estimation round.
The Estimator desires the ability to change their estimate, view prior estimates, and utilize a countdown timer to facilitate focused discussions and reach consensus.
The Participant aims to see who has given estimates and receive immediate notifications of new estimates to stay informed during the game.
The Participant seeks to scroll through previous stories and estimates to inform current estimations and discussions.
The Participant desires to see thumbnail photos and consistent card order to enhance the personal and predictable nature of the game.
The User expects the application to respond quickly to actions, provide user-friendly error pages, and utilize sensible URLs for a logical and transparent experience.
The User aims to use Unicode characters within the application to support various languages.
The Researcher aims to access non-identifiable game results to study patterns and behaviors in estimation processes.
lowLevelGoals: The Moderator can initiate a new game session by providing a name or other initial parameters.
The Moderator can send invitations to estimators and participants to join an active game session.
The Moderator can initiate the estimation process for a selected item, making it visible to estimators.
The Moderator can conclude an estimation round, displaying all submitted estimates to the participants.
The Moderator can input details for a new item (e.g., story, task) that needs to be estimated.
The Moderator can modify the description, title, or other attributes of an item already added to the game.
The Moderator can remove an item from the current game's list of items to be estimated.
The Moderator can reset the estimates for a specific item and start a new estimation round for it.
The Moderator can mark an item's estimation as complete and record the agreed-upon estimate.
The Moderator can upload a file or connect to an external system to import multiple stories or tasks into the game.
The Moderator can view a historical record of all past estimation sessions.
The Moderator can download a detailed report of a completed game, including items, estimates, and discussions.
The Moderator can register for a new account by providing necessary credentials.
The Moderator can access their account by entering their username and password.
The Moderator can update their profile information, such as name, email, or other preferences.
The Moderator can update their password to a new one.
The Moderator can initiate a process to recover or reset their forgotten password.
The Moderator can permanently remove their account and associated data from the system.
The Moderator can choose from predefined estimation scales (e.g., Fibonacci, T-shirt sizes) for a new or ongoing game.
The Moderator can define how many estimators must submit their estimates before revealing results or moving forward.
The Estimator can enter a game session using an invitation link or game ID.
The Estimator can see the details and description of the item currently being estimated.
The Estimator can select and submit their chosen estimate value for the active item.
The Estimator can see a comprehensive list of all stories or tasks planned for estimation in the current game.
The Estimator can view indicators showing who among the participants has already submitted their estimate for the current item.
The Estimator can see if the round is active, paused, or completed, and if estimates have been revealed.
The Estimator can modify their estimate for the current item before the round is closed.
The Estimator can see the estimates submitted by all participants once the moderator reveals them.
The Estimator can see a visual timer indicating the remaining time for discussion during an estimation round.
The Participant can see a visual indication of which team members have submitted their estimates for the current item.
The Participant gets an alert or visual cue when another participant submits an estimate.
The Participant can navigate through a list of items that have already been estimated in the current or past games.
The Participant can see the final estimates or individual estimates for items from previous rounds or games.
The Participant can see small profile pictures or avatars of other participants in the game.
The Participant observes that the estimation cards (e.g., Fibonacci numbers) are always presented in the same sequence.
The User observes that the application responds instantly to clicks, hovers, and other interactions.
The User sees clear, understandable messages when an error occurs, guiding them on how to proceed.
The User finds that the web addresses (URLs) for different sections of the application are structured in an intuitive and easy-to-understand manner.
The User can type and display characters from different languages and scripts within text fields.
The Researcher can retrieve game data where all personally identifiable information has been removed.
The Researcher can apply filters (e.g., date range, game type, estimation scale) to narrow down the dataset for analysis.
